attributes.body:
そんなに, like そんな, is one of the most common ways to express that one thing is 'like' something else in casual conversation. The addition of the particle に just highlights そんな as being the 'destination' of the 'like' amount. This construction is regularly translated as 'so much', 'that much', or simply 'like that'.

As a word, そんなに is used adverbially. This means that it may come before any verb, い-Adjective, or な-Adjective.

Almost any そんなに based sentence can be translated literally as 'to an extent like (A)', where (A) is the word that comes after そんなに, and に indicates 'to'.

As そんなに is another example of こそあど言葉（ことば） (words like これ, それ, あれ, and どれ), it means that こんなに, あんなに, and どんなに may also be used.

Despite this, そんなに is almost considered a set phrase, and is therefore the most common out of all of the possibilities (except for どんなに, which is often used when explaining/giving reasons for something).

attributes.description: How to use こんな・そんな・ あんな
Adverbial そんなに vs. Adjectival そんな

attributes.body: Both あまり～ない and そんなに express a negative degree, but with different nuance. あまり～ない means 'not very' in a general sense, e.g. あまり寒くない ('It's not very cold.'). そんなに (literally 'that much') can imply comparison to a standard and can be used with both negative and affirmative phrases, e.g. そんなに好きなら 'if you like [it] that much...' and そんなに好きじゃない ('I don't like it that much.').

attributes.body: そんな・こんな・あんな・どんな come before nouns and mean 'that/this/what kind of (A)' or 'something like (A)'. そんなに is the same そんな, but followed by に. そんなに (as well as こんなに, あんなに, どんなに) is used with verbs or adjectives to add emphasis, similar to 'that much' or 'to that extent' in English. For example, そんな本 means 'a book/books like that,' and そんなに面白い means 'that interesting' or 'so interesting'.
